items.stem: In Zig, what does the try keyword do when applied to an expression that returns an error union?

options.text: It unwraps the success value, or returns the error from the current function if one occurred
options.rationale: Correct: try is shorthand for 'catch |e| return e', propagating errors upward.

options.text: It ignores any error and continues
options.rationale: try does not ignore errors; it propagates them.

options.text: It retries the expression until it succeeds
options.rationale: There is no retry; try handles the error-union result once.

options.text: It converts the error into null
options.rationale: That is closer to optionals; try returns the error, it does not nullify it.

items.explanation: Correct: try is shorthand for 'catch |e| return e', propagating errors upward.

items.stem: Which statements about memory management in Zig are correct? (Select TWO)

options.text: Heap allocation is explicit and goes through an allocator you pass in
options.rationale: Correct: Zig has no hidden global allocator; callers provide one.

options.text: defer schedules cleanup (such as freeing) to run when the scope exits
options.rationale: Correct: defer runs its statement on scope exit, pairing allocation with release.

options.text: Zig uses a garbage collector to reclaim memory automatically
options.rationale: Zig has no garbage collector; memory is managed manually via allocators.

options.text: Freeing memory is unnecessary because the runtime tracks it
options.rationale: There is no such runtime tracking; unfreed memory leaks.

items.explanation: Correct: Zig has no hidden global allocator; callers provide one.; Correct: defer runs its statement on scope exit, pairing allocation with release.

options.text: A pointer together with a length, giving a bounds-checked view of contiguous elements
options.rationale: Correct: a slice carries both a pointer and a len, enabling safe iteration and bounds checks.

options.text: A single raw pointer with no length information
options.rationale: That is a plain pointer; a slice also carries a length.
Zig has no garbage collection; a slice is just ptr plus len.

options.text: A compile-time-only type with no runtime representation
options.rationale: Slices exist at runtime as a pointer/length pair.
